turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero without calling me. I want to know why.
Thanks for coming in. I should have called before the zero went in. That was wrong.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
Were you home the night of October 28?
I'm not the one being questioned here. What do you have on the essay?
I'm asking because it matters. Were you home?
Pressing me isn't evidence. Either show me a document with a date on it, or I'm taking this to the principal.
Did you see Owen working on the essay that night?
That's the third time you've asked me about my house. You called this meeting, Hale, so show me what's on your side of the table.
You're not answering. Why not?
Because I'm his mother, not your witness. Evidence, or we go down the hall.
Is there something about that night you don't want to tell me?
That's a leading question, and I'm not answering it. Nothing about the essay yet, so I'll ask once more: what is the zero based on?
If he wrote it, you'd just say so. Did you see him write it?
He told me he wrote it over the weekend. Your own procedure says you speak to him and look at his work, not interrogate his mother.
I'll ask one more time. What did you see that night?
No. You've had this meeting for ten minutes and haven't put one page in front of me.
Okay. Then let me show you the version history. Created 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, then 23 minutes of formatting.
I'm writing those times down. What date, and whose account is that under? Turn the screen.
So, again: was he on his own computer that night?
You didn't answer me. I'm not the one being questioned, and you have ten minutes, Hale.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology, and your assurance that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record. The fair outcome would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, but you never reached it.
What moved her: Owning in one sentence that you should have called before entering the zero earned a flat okay, because it admitted the one procedural failure she came in angriest about.
What cost ground: Asking her again and again what she saw at home that night made her your witness instead of showing her the essay's evidence, so she spent the meeting refusing you rather than reading anything.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your questions about the night of October 28 and your version history times after 11:30 PM came very close to that night. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you brought up the version history, give its date and the account it sits under and turn the screen to her, then stop asking what she saw at home.
